chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, from some of his men, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from a man, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

This group (the Shia) will be closest to Allah and Allah will be most pleased with them when they miss the Proof of Allah, who is hidden from them and does not appear to them, and they do not know his location, yet in that state they know and are certain that the Proof of Allah and His covenant have not been annulled. At that time, expect the deliverance morning and evening, for the bitterest wrath of Allah upon His enemies will be when they miss His Proof and He does not appear to them. And Allah knows that His true believers will not doubt; if He knew that they would doubt, He would not hide His Proof from them for the blink of an eye. And that will not be except with the evil of people.

key_terms.حُجَّةَ اللَّهِ: The Proof of Allah (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of the Shia during the occultation of the Imam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the Shia attain their highest spiritual station during the Major Occultation) by maintaining unwavering conviction in the Imam's continued authority despite his physical absence. This period of 'missing the proof' serves as a rigorous test of faith, distinguishing the steadfast believers from the 'worst of people' who succumb to doubt, thereby intensifying Allah's wrath upon the enemies. The narration underscores that the occultation is a deliberate divine decree to preserve the covenant, not a sign of abandonment.
